limitations: Closed IDs and reviewed whole-source/AST pins are drift checks, not semantic inference or proof of whole-source completeness.
OCaml source regions are manually reviewed anchors. No OCaml parsing, compilation, execution or native witness result is inferred.
Python AST closure includes all syntax calls, including out-of-slice calls; not every call is a contextual rule or a classified semantic call graph.
Complementary syntax and family links preserve identities only; they confer no support status or witness sufficiency.
Both source validators accumulate diagnostics; earlier invalidity does not imply a secondary source branch cannot run. Admitted valid-source preconditions must be explicit.
Three stage differences are source predictions only. Counterexample originals are pinned, but no mutation or semantic checker is executed here.
Source unit/scope predicates outside this slice and every later operational/domain/implementation/material predicate remain open.
